title: Build an Update Scheduler
short_description: Batch reactive jobs and run them through pre, update, and post phases.
description: The starter defines a job with id, pre and disposed flags, plus the main queue structures.
Implement microtask batching, deduplication, deterministic order, watcher timing, and nextTick.
instructions: Complete queueJob(job) so it deduplicates by identity, ignores disposed jobs, and schedules one pending flush.
Sort the queue by ascending id and place a pre job before the update that shares its id.
Complete queuePostJob(job) with a deduplicated queue that runs after the main jobs.
Complete queueWatcher(job, flush, ownerId): sync runs immediately, post uses the post queue, and pre shares its owner id.
Make the flush process jobs added while it is running and check again for work created by the post phase.
Complete nextTick(callback?) so it reuses the current flush promise and supports both await and callback forms.
Keep resetScheduler working so every test starts with empty queues, sets, and indexes.

hints.title: Job identity
hints.body: Use a `Set` beside the queue. Add the job only when that same reference is not already pending.

hints.title: One microtask
hints.body: Store `currentFlushPromise`. Create it with `resolvedPromise.then(flushJobs)` only while it is still `null`.

hints.title: Pre order
hints.body: Compare `id` first. When two jobs share an id, the one with `pre = true` must sort first.

hints.title: Finish the cycle
hints.body: Flush the post phase before setting `currentFlushPromise = null`. If a callback added more work, run another flush before the current promise resolves.
